programme: MEIS1 sits atop a proneural/neural-progenitor specification circuit — its target set includes SOX3, PAX6 and ASCL1 (the core proneural transcription-factor trio that defines neural stem/progenitor identity and the proneural subtype of glioma) plus HIF1A, the master hypoxia-response regulator. ISL1 and POU4F2, LIM- and POU-homeodomain factors from the same eye-field/neural-tube patterning lineage, reinforce this circuit: both converge on PAX6 (POU4F2 targets PAX6 directly; ISL1 targets SHH, PAX6's classical upstream partner in neural patterning). ZBTB20 marks the hypoxic-stress arm specifically in ischemic tissue, where a retrieved paper places it downstream of a hypoxia-ischemia oxidative-stress axis.
role_in_a: In stroke, the relevant edge of this programme is the hypoxia/HIF1A response to ischemia. ZBTB20 is the one factor with direct retrieved evidence here, implicated in hypoxia-ischemia-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress; MEIS1's own HIF1A target places it in the same adaptive-hypoxia signaling that governs peri-infarct tissue survival, though no retrieved paper places MEIS1, ISL1, or POU4F2 in stroke directly.
role_in_b: In glioma, the relevant edge is proneural progenitor-identity reactivation. MEIS1 is directly tied to glioma through a functional enhancer connectome / risk-variant study (PMID 40830415), consistent with its target set (SOX3, ASCL1, PAX6) mapping onto the proneural transcriptional program that defines a major glioma subtype and its stem-like, hypoxia-adapted cells (via HIF1A).
shared_axis: Hypoxia is the physiological bridge: ischemic stroke tissue and the glioblastoma core are both profoundly hypoxic microenvironments. MEIS1 links a neural-progenitor specification module (SOX3/PAX6/ASCL1, reinforced by ISL1 and POU4F2 converging on the same PAX6/SHH circuit) to HIF1A-driven hypoxic signaling, while ZBTB20 marks the same hypoxia-stress arm on the stroke side — so the two diseases could share this programme via convergent hypoxic reactivation of a normally dormant neurodevelopmental progenitor circuit rather than via a common cell of origin.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors' own target sets (PAX6/SHH/ASCL1/HIF1A convergence), and the retrieved record independently places MEIS1 in glioma and ZBTB20 in stroke-hypoxia — but ISL1 and POU4F2, despite high recurrence (42/69 and 37/69), have no retrieved literature support in either disease, so the disease-bridging claim rests mainly on established general biology (HIF1A in ischemia; proneural TFs in glioma) rather than on documented cross-disease evidence.
support: PMID 39869050 — links ZBTB20 to hypoxia-ischemia-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, placing it in a stroke-relevant hypoxic-injury pathway; PMID 40830415 — ties MEIS1 to functional enhancer connectomes and risk variants in human glioma, placing it directly in disease B.
how_to_falsify: Knock down MEIS1 in a proneural-subtype glioma stem-cell line and assay SOX3/ASCL1/PAX6 expression and HIF1A stabilization under hypoxia; in parallel, knock down ZBTB20 in a mouse MCAO ischemic-stroke model and measure infarct volume and peri-infarct HIF1A/oxidative-stress markers. If MEIS1 loss does not reduce proneural marker expression or hypoxic HIF1A response in glioma cells, or ZBTB20 loss has no effect on the hypoxic-injury phenotype in stroke tissue, the shared hypoxia-progenitor axis account fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|brain: stroke's hypoxic injury arises in vascularized peri-infarct neural tissue while glioma's hypoxia arises within tumor parenchyma, so any shared axis operates in anatomically and mechanistically distinct compartments. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 69 patient-group comparisons, limiting true replication despite the high comparison count. Eight of the twelve listed factors (FOXS1, FOXN1, ETV1, ZNF281, CDX2, FOXA3, RFX3, TBPL1) are lineage-specifying TFs for unrelated tissues (intestine, liver/lung, thymus, prostate/GIST, cilia/interneurons, neural crest, testis) with no clear fit to this programme and are deliberately excluded from carrying_factors — forcing them in would overreach. TBPL1 and FOXS1 in particular have no retrieved literature in either disease. The single-view exclusions (e.g., GLI1, TCF12) and tissue-generic exclusions (e.g., NOTCH1, FOXP3) were removed before ranking, so this account should not be read as the generic inflammation/Notch-driven stroke-glioma story — that axis was filtered out upstream.
